facts.fact: Marketing Magazine's entry, published October 7, 2014, states that StackAdapt represents 3,000 publishers globally.
facts.quote: The only native programmatic company in Canada, StackAdapt represents 3,000 publishers globally, and has worked on campaigns for Ford, GE and Sport Chek.

facts.fact: According to Marketing Magazine's 2014 entry, the StackAdapt platform rolled out in spring 2014 under the name Collective Roll and had grown to 15 staff with a US office.
facts.quote: The StackAdapt platform rolled out in spring 2014 (then under the name Collective Roll), and has since grown to 15 staff and launched a US office.

facts.fact: Per Marketing Magazine's 2014 entry, co-founder Vitaly Pecherskiy and Ildar Shar left WPP in 2013 to investigate the banner ad problem.
facts.quote: Pecherskiy and Shar left WPP in 2013 to investigate the problem, together with Yang Han

facts.fact: Marketing Magazine's 2014 entry says StackAdapt has roped several thousand publishers into adding its native units to their sites, including Songza, Jango and The Christian Post.
facts.quote: Since then he’s roped several thousand publishers into adding StackAdapt’s native units to their sites, like Songza, Jango and The Christian Post.

facts.fact: StackAdapt's native ad unit adapts its font, size, colour scheme and content to the surrounding site, with advertisers' raw text and images poured into a publisher-designed template.
facts.quote: Their solution was a native ad unit that adapts all its parameters—font, size, colour scheme, even content—to the content around it.
